bib.title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance

legacy_report:
SOURCE: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance. Wu, Irsoy, Lu, Dabravolski, Dredze, Gehrmann, Kambadur, Rosenberg, Mann. Preprint, arXiv:2303.17564v3, 21 Dec 2023. The PDF prints no venue.

COVERAGE: 204,766 of 204,766 chars, all 76 pages, read in contiguous ranges. References were read only for origins. To stay near the length limit, per-task rows are omitted for BIG-bench Hard (Table 13, p27), knowledge (Table 14, p28), linguistic tasks (Table 17, p30) and NER (Table 12, p25). Their aggregates are below. I read figure captions only and did not view the plots.

CLAIMS

Corpus, model and training
- claim: The corpus is about half private finance text and half public text, each deduplicated.
  number: 363B domain (51.27%) + 345B public (48.73%) = 709B tokens
  setup: FinPile docs dated 2007-03-01 to 2022-07-31; Web 298B, News 38B, Filings 14B, Press 9B, Bloomberg 5B; public is Pile 184B, C4 138B, Wikipedia 24B; dedup follows Lee et al. (2022a)
  quote: "FinPile 175,886 1,017 17,883 4.92 3,635 51.27%" / "PUBLIC 50,744 3,314 16,818 4.87 3,454 48.73%" / "TOTAL 226,631 1,531 34,701 4.89 7,089 100.00%" (token column is in units of 1e8)
  where: Table 1, p6; dates p7
- claim: Training stopped before one full pass because validation loss had stalled.
  number: 139,200 steps, about 53 days, 569B of 709B tokens, about 80% of an epoch
  setup: the run continued to step 146,000; the final checkpoint was chosen by validation loss and downstream evaluations
  quote: "We trained for a total of 139,200 steps ( ⁄tildelow53 days) and ended model training after completing ⁄tildelow80% of one epoch through our training data (569B tokens out of the 709B tokens available)."
  where: §4, p16
- claim: The authors concede that longer training might have helped.
  number: none
  setup: same run
  quote: "although it’s possible that substantially longer training may have yielded further improvements."
  where: §4, p16
- claim: The model is BLOOM-style, decoder-only and sized at about 50B parameters.
  number: 50.6B (exact 50,558,868,480); 70 layers, 40 heads, D=7,680, FFN 30,720
  setup: ALiBi, GELU, tied embeddings, extra LayerNorm after embeddings; the shape comes from the Levine et al. (2020) formula (target D=7510, rounded for head divisibility and multiples of 8)
  quote: "Number of Layers 70 / Number of Heads 40 / Vocabulary Size 131,072 / Hidden Dimension 7,680 / Total Parameters 50.6B" (table rows joined with /)
  where: Table 4, p11; A.5, p64
- claim: Hardware was 512 A100s on AWS, using ZeRO stage 3 through a proprietary library.
  number: 64 × 8 A100 40GB; 32.5 s/step; 102 TFLOPs average; 2.36e23 total FLOPs
  setup: SageMaker p4d.24xlarge with the SMP library; model sharded across 128 GPUs with 4 copies; activation checkpointing per layer; MiCS; fused kernels gave 4-5 TFLOPs
  quote: "We shard a model across 128 GPUs, and we have 4 copies of the model during training." and "Hardware 64 × 8 A100 40GB / Throughput 32.5 sec/step / avg. TFLOPs 102 / total FLOPS 2.36e23"
  where: Table 4, p11; §3.4, p14
- claim: Compute budget and Chinchilla fits put the model near optimal size but short of data.
  number: 1.3M GPU hours; fits of 52.993B/1111.112B and 49.753B/1175.766B (params/tokens); about 30% buffer
  setup: 0.75 × 1.3M was plugged in because checkpointing adds 0.33x; FinPile was kept at no less than half of training
  quote: "We start with a total compute budget of 1.3M GPU hours on 40GB A100 GPUs." and "leave ⁄tildelow30% of the total compute budget as a buffer for unforeseen failures, retries, and restarts."
  where: §3.2, p12-13
- claim: Chinchilla laws may not transfer across tokenizers, and the authors leave that open.
  number: none
  setup: footnote 1
  quote: "The scaling law derived by Chinchilla is tokenizer-specific."
  where: p12
- claim: They used a Unigram tokenizer with a large vocabulary, trained on the Pile.
  number: 131,072 tokens (2^17), against about 50,000 standard
  setup: 5,632 sub-tokenizers (22 domains × 256 chunks, each 65,536 tokens) merged into 7M, then pruned; vocabularies of 25,000-550,000 compared by encoded C4 size, optimum 125,000, rounded up
  quote: "This gives us a vocabulary size of 125,000, which we then round up to the nearest power of 2 (217, or 131,072 tokens)."
  where: §2.3, p10 (the extraction renders 2^17 as "217")
- claim: The tokenizer needs fewer tokens than competitors on the public data, but not everywhere.
  number: others use 113-126% as many on public data; BLOOM uses 88% on Wikipedia
  setup: older FinPile version; the Total row sums public sets only (excludes FinPile)
  quote: "Total 390 113% 408 118% 434 126% 345" and "Wikipedia 21 88% 23 99% 24 103% 24"
  where: Table 3, p10
- claim: Optimizer and batch recipe.
  number: AdamW β1 0.9, β2 0.95, weight decay 0.1; LR 6e-5 to 6e-6; 1800-step warmup; batch 1,024 then 2,048; 2,048-token sequences; clip 0.3
  setup: final v2 configuration; BF16 forward and backward, parameters stored and updated in FP32, loss softmax in FP32
  quote: "in the first 7,200 steps, we use a batch size of 1,024 (2.1M tokens), then switch to a batch size of 2,048 (4.2M tokens) for the remainder of training."
  where: §3.3, p13; mixed precision p15

Tried and abandoned (Appendix C)
- claim: v0 ordered data by month as curriculum learning, stalled, and was abandoned without a diagnosis.
  number: stuck about one week in; little progress after step 20k
  setup: oldest data first (2007), validation from 2022; replaced by shuffling
  quote: "We were unable to ascertain if curriculum learning had a negative impact on training or if the loss plateaued due to other factors"
  where: C.0, p67-68
- claim: In v1.0 gradient norms grew from about 12k steps, and four fix attempts failed.
  number: about 12k steps (about 4.5 days); LR 1e-4 cut to 8e-5 and 6e-5; clip 1.0 cut to 0.3; FP32 LM head
  setup: runs v1.1-v1.4, some rolled back to step 10.8k
  quote: "the gradient norm showed a steady increase after about 12k steps (⁄tildelow4.5 days of training), with occasional spikes"
  where: C.1, p68-69
- claim: Component-level monitoring isolated the problem to Input LayerNorm at layer 1, and also exposed a weight-decay bug inherited from BERT code.
  number: elbow at about 12k steps
  setup: decay was applied to LayerNorm multipliers initialised at 1; the authors say this does not explain the elbow
  quote: "Weight decay was applied to all the non-bias parameters, as opposed to skipping the LayerNorm multiplier weight γ since they are initialized at 1."
  where: C.1, p70
- claim: They restarted from scratch (v2.0) with about ten conservative changes at once and got a stable run, but cannot say which change mattered.
  number: about 42 days to about 115,500 iterations; one restart at 28 days for a platform job limit
  setup: LR 6e-5, clip 0.3, FP32 LM head, full shuffle, new seed, LN_em restored, longer warmup, no decay on γ, Megatron init rescaling, query key scaling, batch warmup
  quote: "we cannot conclude which of these changes was decisive in leading to a successful training run."
  where: C.2, p71-72
- claim: After validation loss stalled, runs v2.1-v2.6 varied LR, dropout and weight decay, and none clearly helped.
  number: v2 flat from 115,500 to 133,200; weight decay 0.01 gave almost the same curve as 0.1
  setup: rollback of 7 days plus re-shuffling; second validation set val_past added; MMLU and BBH subset used as checks
  quote: "We did not observe that any particular change significantly improved the downstream evaluations and validation loss (Table 20)."
  where: C.3, p72-75
- claim: Selected step 139,200 gained little over the pre-intervention checkpoint.
  number: val_future perplexity 8.30 to 8.14; MMLU 38.79 to 39.02; BBH subset 43.10 to 44.20
  setup: 105M-token validation sets; the extraction lost run columns, so the run per row is not printed
  quote: "115500 8.30 8.43" / "139200 8.14 8.32" / "115500 38.79 43.10" / "139200 39.02 44.20"
  where: Table 20, p76
- claim: A single month of validation data may have misled decisions, as the authors admit.
  number: roughly 105M tokens
  setup: val_future is July 2022 only; val_past came from the end of the training set and is not time-held-out
  quote: "it was possible that a single month of data was not properly reflective of the model’s abilities"
  where: C.3, p73

Benchmarks (BloombergGPT / GPT-NeoX / OPT 66B / BLOOM 176B, plus GPT-3 or PaLM where noted)
- claim: Public finance tasks: best on four of five, second on NER.
  number: average 62.51 vs 51.90, 53.01, 54.35; win rate 0.93
  setup: F1 (FPB, FiQA SA, Headline, NER); exact match (ConvFinQA); 5-shot, NER 20-shot
  quote: "ConvFinQA 43.41 30.06 27.88 36.31 / FiQA SA 75.07 50.59 51.60 53.12 / FPB 51.07 44.64 48.67 50.25 / Headline 82.20 73.22 79.41 76.51 / NER 60.82 60.98 57.49 55.56 / All Tasks (avg) 62.51 51.90 53.01 54.35 / All Tasks (WR) 0.93 0.27 0.33 0.47"
  where: Table 8, p21
- claim: Internal aspect sentiment shows the widest gap, except on social media.
  number: average 62.47 vs 29.23, 35.76, 33.39; win rate 1.00
  setup: 5-shot weighted F1; up to 1k test examples; private data; the unlabeled text likely occurs in FinPile
  quote: "Equity News 79.63 14.17 20.98 19.96 / Equity Social Media 72.40 66.48 71.36 68.04 / Equity Transcript 65.06 25.08 37.58 34.82 / ES News 46.12 26.99 31.44 28.07 / Country News 49.14 13.45 17.41 16.06 / All Tasks (avg) 62.47 29.23 35.76 33.39"
  where: Table 10, p23; caveat p22
- claim: Internal NER: the larger BLOOM wins. Joint NER+NED: BloombergGPT wins on average.
  number: NER 62.63 vs 59.75, 58.09, 64.83 (WR 0.57 vs BLOOM 0.95); NER+NED 64.83 vs 39.26, 58.79, 45.43 (WR 0.95)
  setup: seven internal sets, 20-shot F1, 500 test examples each; described as exploratory; NED labels come from a separate entity-linking system
  quote: "All Tasks (avg) 62.63 59.75 58.09 64.83 / All Tasks (WR) 0.57 0.29 0.19 0.95" and "All Tasks (avg) 64.83 39.26 58.79 45.43 / All Tasks (WR) 0.95 0.00 0.67 0.38"
  where: Table 12, p25
- claim: General benchmarks: beats similar-sized models but trails larger ones or reported GPT-3 on most averages.
  number: BBH 41.97 vs 40.25, 39.58, 44.91, PaLM 52.3; knowledge 66.50 vs 63.10, 64.95, 67.01; MMLU 39.18 vs 35.95, 35.99, 39.13, GPT-3 43.9; reading 61.22 vs 42.81, 50.21, 49.37, GPT-3 67.0; linguistic 60.63 vs 57.18, 58.59, 58.26, GPT-3 63.4
  setup: BBH 3-shot; knowledge 1-shot; MMLU 5-shot; reading and linguistic 1-shot; accuracy; GPT-3 and PaLM numbers are reported elsewhere, not rerun
  quote: "All Tasks (avg) 41.97 40.25 39.58 44.91 52.3" / "All Tasks (avg) 66.50 63.10 64.95 67.01 -" / "Average 39.18 35.95 35.99 39.13 43.9" / "All Tasks (avg) 61.22 42.81 50.21 49.37 67.0" / "All Tasks (avg) 60.63 57.18 58.59 58.26 63.4"
  where: Tables 13-17, p27-30
- claim: The comparison cohort differs in tokens, size and compute.
  number: 569B/50.6B/1.00× vs NeoX 472/20/0.33×, OPT 300/66/0.69×, BLOOM 366/176/2.24×, GPT-3 300/175/1.82×
  setup: authors call compute only partly comparable, since BLOOM data is 1/3 English and OPT repeated data
  quote: "BloombergGPT 569 50.6 1.00 × / GPT-NeoX 472 20 0.33 × / OPT 300 66 0.69 × / BLOOM 366 176 2.24 × / GPT-3 300 175 1.82 ×"
  where: Table 6, p17
- claim: The authors rank the causes of the results by impact, without an ablation.
  number: none
  setup: conclusion
  quote: "We attribute this, in decreasing order of impact, to 1. a well-curated internal dataset, 2. our unique choice in tokenizer, and 3. an up-to-date architecture."
  where: §9, p39

LIMITS
- No ablation: no public-only or finance-only twin, and no same-model run with another tokenizer. The causal ranking above is untested. Tokenizer effects are listed as future work (p39).
- Neither model nor data is released. Quote: "While we cannot release FinPile" (p7). The stated reason is that weight access could expose the data: "providing access to model weights entails giving access to FinPile" (p38). The release risk also covers imitation abuse.
- Internal benchmarks are private, so those results cannot be checked. Likely data overlap with FinPile is conceded for the internal sets (p22).
- Evaluation choices: the number of shots was chosen for best average across models (p20); the best of three classification methods is reported per model and task (p18). Non-LLM finance models are excluded, so claims cover LLMs only (p20). No error bars or seed counts are printed.
- Toxicity and bias are unmeasured, "unknown as yet" (p39).
- Not shown: dollar cost and GPU hours actually consumed. Total calendar time across failed runs is also not given.
- The model never saw all its data. C.3 cites 77% used and budget nearly exhausted (p75).
- Dated: LLaMA is excluded from comparison for lack of access or third-party results (footnote 2, p18). Training data stops July 2022. Figure 6's footnote shows stale-knowledge risk in another model. Future work lists SwiGLU, RoPE and query/key normalization (p75).

BUILDS ON: BLOOM (Scao et al., 2022; Le Scao et al., 2022); Chinchilla (Hoffmann et al., 2022); Kaplan et al. (2020); Levine et al. (2020); dedup, Lee et al. (2022a); Unigram, Kudo (2018), Kudo and Richardson (2018), Bostrom and Durrett (2020); byte handling, Radford et al. (2019); digit chunks, PaLM (Chowdhery et al., 2022); GPT-3 settings (Brown et al., 2020); AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019); ZeRO (Rajbhandari et al., 2020); SMP (Karakus et al., 2021); MiCS (Zhang et al., 2022b); checkpointing (Chen et al., 2016); Megatron-LM (Shoeybi et al., 2019); OPT chronicles (Zhang et al., 2022a); FLUE (Shah et al., 2022); HELM (Liang et al., 2022); BBH (Suzgun et al., 2022).

CODE
- Pretokenization regex, §2.3, p9: `[ A-Za-z]+|[0-9]|[^A-Za-z0-9]+`
- Shape rule, §3.2, p13: `D = exp(5.039) exp(0.0555 · L)`
- Probability-merge rule, p10 (prose): merged "by taking a weighted average of the probabilities of corresponding tokens"

FIGURES (pages match printed numbers)
- Fig 1, p12: "Kaplan et al. (2020) and Chinchilla scaling laws with prior large language model and BloombergGPT parameter and data sizes." Shows the model on the size and token curves at a glance.
- Fig 2, p15: "(Smoothed) training and validation losses for BloombergGPT." One plot shows the batch-size kink and each late intervention.
- Fig 3, p19: "Bits per byte on a heldout test set of each data type in our FinPile." Shows the per-source gap, largest for Filings. Values are not printed in the text.
- Fig 7, p67: "Learning curve of our first training attempt named v0." Shows the curriculum plateau.
- Fig 8, p68: "Gradient norms (top) and train & validation loss (bottom) of v1.x runs." Shows gradient jumps aligned with loss jumps.
- Fig 9, p69: "Rescaled norms for each component in v1.0 run. Input LayerNorm at Layer 1 stood out." Shows the diagnostic method.
- Fig 12, p73: "Loss values for various runs at the end of v2." Shows that every rescue attempt flattens.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- The paper disagrees with itself, and I report rather than resolve these:
  1. §4 says about 80% of an epoch (569/709); C.3 says "we had used 77% of our training data" (p75).
  2. p23 says "four internal" sentiment tasks and gaps of "at least 25" points on "the other three", but Table 10 has five tasks. ES News beats the next model by only 14.68 (46.12 vs 31.44, my arithmetic).
  3. p26 says that on social media NER+NED it is second "behind BLOOM176B", but Table 12 shows OPT 70.57 first, BloombergGPT 67.34, BLOOM 65.94.
  4. p26 says "by a large margin", yet Filings is 66.67 vs OPT 65.63 and Transcripts 73.15 vs 70.44.
  5. p4 says forty years of collection, p5 says two decades, and the documents span 2007-2022.
- Extraction faults: "~" renders as "⁄tildelow"; spaced headings ("T raining"); exponents flatten ("217"); Appendix A math is scrambled; the Appendix C heading icons are lost; table columns in Tables 19-20 are collapsed.
- The target note /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/01-llm-fundamentals/notes/06-pretraining-data-and-objectives.md does not list arXiv:2303.17564 in its sources.
